criteria.name: Track fit & prize odds
criteria.justification: Clearly targets constrained fleet coordination, with a compelling failure-and-recovery demonstration. Strong host-specific presentation, but the orchestration is a synchronous simulation rather than independently running workers, limiting its technical distinction.

criteria.name: Relevance to Base Power
criteria.justification: Directly addresses VPP dispatch, unavailable devices, customer backup reserves, and market opportunity. The reserve tradeoff is concrete and reproducible, although no actual telemetry or device integration is demonstrated.

criteria.name: Technical depth
criteria.justification: Proportional allocation and redistribution correctly enforce the modeled energy and power constraints. Cached values matched corresponding entries in the official [ERCOT feed](https://www.ercot.com/api/1/services/read/dashboards/system-wide-prices.json). However, every request regenerates the fleet; there is no evolving state, asynchronous failure detection, acknowledgment handling, or optimization across time. The parser also accepted a stale, incomplete feed with an invalid interval string.

criteria.name: It actually works
criteria.justification: Started successfully using python3 app.py without application dependencies; all 27 tests passed. Browser walkthrough completed without JavaScript errors in live and forced-offline cached modes. Verified 7.489 → 6.362 → 7.489 MW recovery, the 50% reserve scenario, 5,000 homes, invalid-input rejection, and a truthful 2.104 MW shortfall under 50% failure. Servers were stopped afterward.

criteria.name: Commercial clarity
criteria.justification: Names fleet operators and dispatch engineers, identifies a credible operational problem, and illustrates gross opportunity value. It does not establish a differentiated buying proposition, customer validation, pricing, or measured improvement over an existing dispatch approach. Synthetic scarcity revenue is not demonstrated commercial return.

criteria.name: Demo & pitch quality
criteria.justification: Polished dashboard, coherent three-minute script, clear simulation labels, and reproducible headline numbers. The 50% reserve example honestly exposes 252 homes already below the requested floor. Claims about proving the difficult coordination loop and simply swapping in production telemetry overstate the demonstrated integration readiness; cached timestamps also omit the date in the UI.

summary: A polished, reliable, highly relevant hackathon prototype. Strong demonstration and constraint handling make it competitive, but modest coordination depth and unvalidated commercial differentiation keep it below a clear winner.
strengths: One-command startup, no application dependencies, and 27 passing tests.
Verified browser demo works with live data and offline fallback.
Recovery and capacity shortfalls behave correctly in tested scenarios.
Clear backup-reserve tradeoff with honest reporting of existing deficits.
weaknesses: Independent workers and failure detection are simulated inside one synchronous calculation.
No persistent fleet evolution or dispatch optimization across intervals.
Feed validation does not establish freshness, complete coverage, or valid interval timestamps.
Commercial value lacks customer validation and comparative evidence.
